explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/366: 'Are there any 2-full n such that n+1 is 3-full? That is, if p | n then p² | n and if p | n+1 then p³ | n+1.' The Lean statement ∃ n > 0, Nat.Full 2 n ∧ Nat.Full 3 (n+1), where Nat.Full k n means p^k ∣ n for every prime factor p of n, is the positive form of the yes/no question. The restriction n > 0 is essential and present: n = 0 would be a trivial witness (0 is k-full for all k, and 1 is vacuously 3-full). Faithful.
